newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Put volume suggest fears of FTSE pullback.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Put volume suggest fears of FTSE pullback.

text.p: Concerns about a pullback in the FTSE 100 -- which rose to yet another record peak again on Monday -- appear to be growing based on options activity, some derivatives dealers said.
They noted a preponderance of trading volume in puts on the FTSE 100 index, which could reflect expectations that the index may be poised to fall from its lofty levels.
"There's a lot of speculation that the market is in for a big correction and that (put volume) may mean that people are taking cover in case we get it," said one dealer.
Most of the volume in the American-style index options was in the December 4050 puts, the December 3850 puts and the November 3900 puts.
At 1400 GMT, total volume in American-style FTSE 100 puts was roughly eight times that of calls.
Put volume exceeded call volume in European-style FTSE options, but by a lesser degree.
The FTSE 100 was up 5.8 points at 4,058.9, having climbed to another record at 4,065.7 earlier.
In equity options, dealers noted that 500 November 460 calls on B.A.T Industries were purchased at 4p.

B.A.T shares, down 10p to 421p after U.S. scientists published a report detailing new evidence of a direct link between smoking and lung cancer, would have to rise more than 35p before November expiry for the calls to be profitable.
Elsewhere, 500 January 1100 Shell Transport calls were sold at 13-1/2p.

The shares were up 7p to 1044-1/2p after having set a record at 1058p as crude oil prices rose. The shares also were bolstered by expectations U.S. oil companies will report healthy quarterly profits this afternoon. Shell is expected to report its third quarter results on October 31.
